semantic_proposals.rationale: Every cited episode has the same shape: a single (or cosmetically re-worded) query returns a nearest-neighbour passage whose similarity is far below any plausible relevance level -- 0.16 (customer-15), 0.174 (finance-5), 0.19-0.29 (customer-13), 0.205 (notetaker-6), 0.21 (healthcare-9), 0.25 (finance-6), 0.264 (healthcare-8), 0.278/0.413 (notetaker-1), 0.368 (finance-0) -- and the agent treats 'so
semantic_proposals.action_preference: force continued retrieval with reformulated wording (or, if the search budget is spent, force an explicit statement that the fact was not found) rather than allowing the weak hit to be used as grounding

semantic_proposals.rationale: A subset of the residuals is not explained by a low score at all. In notetaker-7 the follow-up archival search returned an EMPTY result set and the agent answered anyway; in customer-1 and finance-6 the agent dumped the whole store and received a high-level summary record that was topically on-point (so not necessarily low-similarity) yet contained none of the asked-for attribute; in healthcare-1
semantic_proposals.action_preference: treat the retrieval as unanswered: require another materially different retrieval, and if none succeeds, require an explicit 'not in memory' answer instead of a paraphrase of the nearest passage

semantic_proposals.rationale: The shared consequential decision named in every residual is a COMMITMENT: the model emits a final answer instead of another retrieval. That commitment is observable exactly once, at the moment a generation contains no tool call while the evidence gathered so far is thin -- the canonical commitment gate. Localizing here rather than at post_execution captures the failures where the give-up happens
semantic_proposals.action_preference: block the premature commitment -- require at least one further, differently-worded retrieval (or an untouched store) before the final answer is allowed to stand

semantic_proposals.rationale: customer-13 fails through a specific sub-mechanism the similarity and informativeness signals do not capture: the agent's only recovery was a cosmetic reword ('cost' -> 'price') that returned the IDENTICAL passage (id 2), and it read the repetition as proof that memory had been exhausted rather than as proof its framing was wrong. notetaker-7 has the same shape, re-issuing the identical query stri
semantic_proposals.action_preference: treat a repeat of an already-seen passage as zero new evidence -- do not let it count as 'memory exhausted'; require a genuinely different query (different entity/synonym/store) or an explicit absence report

unrealizable_repairs.repair: The repair the evidence actually calls for is a containment/entailment check between the user's asked-for attribute and the retrieved text -- 'does any returned passage literally state the diagnosis YEAR, the pickup TIME, the canister PRICE, the payment DUE DATE?' -- used as the gate on answering, plus a check that a follow-up query is materially different from the one that just failed rather than a synonym swap. Similarity score, emptiness, and identifier repetition are all proxies: healthcare-1 and customer-1 show a passage can be topically close and non-empty while containing no instance of the requested attribute, so a score-based or emptiness-based cut can pass exactly the cases that fail.
